facts.text: Before settlers arrived, the Cherokee used the Allred area as a hunting ground and kept small villages in the Upper Cumberland region.
Allred takes its name from Jonathan Allred, a North Carolina pioneer who settled the land in the early 1800s.
Jonathan and his relative Theophilus Allred established homesteads along the West Fork River, and the community grew around their land claims.
The 1904 opening of the Overton County Railroad linked Allred to Livingston and Algood, making travel and trade far easier.
Allred’s low‑density rural setting encourages sustainable forestry and agriculture, reflecting the community’s long‑standing connection to the forested terrain.
